summary.text: James Uthmeier is the Republican Attorney General of Florida, appointed in 2025, and won election to a full term on November 3, 2026.
He previously served as Gov. Ron DeSantis's chief of staff and general counsel; in 2026 his office sued Discord over child safety and announced arrests in a statewide election-crimes operation.

paragraphs.text: Uthmeier grew up in Destin and earned undergraduate and graduate degrees from the University of Florida and a law degree from Georgetown University Law Center.
He began his career as a litigation associate at Jones Day in Washington, D.C., and is an adjunct professor at the University of Florida Levin College of Law.
Uthmeier served in the U.S. Department of Commerce as senior counsel and senior advisor from 2017 to 2019.

He then joined Gov. DeSantis's office as deputy general counsel in 2019 and general counsel in 2020, and was chief of staff from October 2021 to August 2023, after which he managed DeSantis's 2024 presidential campaign.
DeSantis appointed Uthmeier Attorney General in February 2025.

James Uthmeier won election to a full term in the November 3, 2026 general election for attorney general with 50.9% of the vote to José Rodriguez's 49.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
On October 1, 2026, his office sued Pfizer and its chairman and CEO in St. Lucie County, alleging deceptive marketing of the company's COVID-19 vaccine; Pfizer said the allegations have no merit.

On October 7, 2026, he filed a motion in Florida's state-court case against Meta seeking an injunction limiting minors' access to its social media apps, and Florida did not join the 47-state settlement with Meta announced in August.
